_: Slice 4, the shell half: the gate itself, and the surface it reaches for
on a machine with no screen.
The claim every one of these tests: the away branch can only ever refuse
what confirm.sh already refused. Before it existed, a runtime with no
moe-confirm and no /usr/bin/osascript exited 1 for every message. So the
bar is not 'does it approve when it should' -- it is 'is there any
arrangement of files and answers that approves when a person did not'.
A NOTE ON BOUNDING, and it is the sixth way a round can look like success.
One of these mutants removes confirm-away.py's 'no ask directory is a
refusal' guard, which sends a test case into an unbounded 3,600-second
poll. On 2026-09-09 that wedged a round for forty minutes; the operator
killed it, and `if False:` was left sitting in the real gate on disk with
nothing failing. A mutation that removes a bound removes the SUITE's bound
with it -- the harness inherits its timeout from the code under test,
which is an oracle derived from the thing it guards, in the time
dimension. scripts/test-confirm-ui.sh's `away()` helper now sets
MOE_ASK_DEADLINE itself so no mutant can take the suite's clock away.
The whole safety argument rests on this line: the away branch is
reached only where the Mac's two dialogs are both absent. Fired
unconditionally, a Mac asks somebody's phone about a dialog it has
already shown them.
mutants.name: the away branch fires on a Mac too
